user_authorization: user approved apt install of gcc-sparc64-linux-gnu and real sparc64 defconfig object compilation of parent/fixed to check loop bounds
purpose: raise the cpumask width premise from host projection to actual sparc64 compiler objects: in the default configuration, do record_one_cpu's num_possible_cpus() and alloc_irqstack_bootmem's for_each_possible_cpu bound read runtime nr_cpu_ids, and does an NR_CPUS=64 control compile them with constant width?

configurations.default: make ARCH=sparc64 sparc64_defconfig, no changes (expected NR_CPUS=4096 from Kconfig default; verified from .config, not assumed)
configurations.nr64: same defconfig then scripts/config --set-val NR_CPUS 64 and olddefconfig; a legal Kconfig value (range 2..4096) used only as width-branch control

builds: 2 revisions x 2 configurations = 4 out-of-tree build directories; targets arch/sparc/kernel/{prom_64,setup_64,smp_64}.o and .i only; no vmlinux, no boot

checks.O1_irqstack_loop_bound: function containing alloc_irqstack_bootmem's loop (setup_arch after inlining, or the function itself) references nr_cpu_ids and a find-bit helper in default; no nr_cpu_ids reference in nr64
checks.O2_record_one_cpu_weight: record_one_cpu references nr_cpu_ids and __bitmap_weight in default; nr64 has no __bitmap_weight call
checks.O3_preprocessed_expansion: .i text of the two functions shows the loop/weight size expression expanded to nr_cpu_ids (default) vs a constant 64 (nr64)
checks.O4_fixed_parent_diff: only fixed record_one_cpu contains the possible-guard comparison; parent smp_64.o contains smp_fill_in_cpu_possible_map

reading_rule: object facts are extracted by objdump relocations/disassembly per symbol; dataflow from the nr_cpu_ids load into the helper size argument is shown as an excerpt for human review, not claimed as automatic dataflow proof
not_claimed: no runtime behaviour, multi-CPU boot, or IRQ-stack fault observation
the candidate remains unconfirmed; object evidence shows which width branch the compiled code takes, not that affected machines exist
stop_rule: failed builds are recorded and not silently retried; any fix is a separate attempt
